No later page shows the pilot query has been run, so it cannot be said whether these placeholders are still open.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the result of the 20-case pilot PACS query. Until then, the textbook carries the sample size as about 1,100 bodies with the case count unknown.

verdicts.quote_a: Records requested 40,000 studies — unconfirmed
verdicts.quote_b: The key is destroyed at study closure or 7 years after IRB approval, whichever is later, per WSU records policy — confirm
verdicts.explanation: The 15 September 2026 draft's open items (40,000 studies unconfirmed, key-destruction period to confirm, trauma co-investigator if agreed, citations to insert) belong to a design the later retrospective protocol replaced. That protocol drops the 2006 window, the fracture and registry aims and the 40,000-study request, and sets key destruction at verified abstraction, no later than acceptance of the publications. Those items no longer hold.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the Retrospective Fluoroscopy Protocol's fields. Mark the September draft as superseded, so its Exempt 4, 2006 window, fracture aim and registry linkage are not copied back in.

verdicts.quote_a: manuscript in preparation for Radiology: Artificial Intelligence
verdicts.quote_b: held from submission pending the technology-transfer office
verdicts.explanation: The handoff of 8 October 2026 lists paper 1 for Radiology: Artificial Intelligence as complete in review and camera-ready copies but held from submission pending the technology-transfer office, with a disclosure submitted on 25 September and no provisional filing recorded. 'In preparation' and 'held from submission' agree that it has not been submitted. The handoff is simply more exact.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the handoff's status: complete, held from submission pending technology transfer, provisional not recorded as of 8 October 2026.

verdicts.quote_a: Until then no word can run.
verdicts.quote_b: The RSNA RATIC download link expires 2026-10-28 02:38 UTC.

verdicts.quote_b: signed and paid for waits on Radiopaedia's countersignature
verdicts.explanation: On 17 October 2026 the atlas has every request letter ready and unsent. Radiopaedia, letter 8, is marked 'Sent: not recorded', with a USD 250 fee from the draft. On 21 October 2026 the grid pipeline says the Radiopaedia licence has been signed and paid for and waits on countersignature, and that spine-datasets has 26 records requested and 5 granted. The atlas's request status no longer holds, at least for Radiopaedia.

verdicts.quote_a: the verified real-frame transitional test count is zero today
verdicts.quote_b: A cross-validation over all 376 patients with transitional anatomy is running now
verdicts.explanation: The cross-validation running on 18 September 2026 was on the data on hand, rendered CT, and the same note says it 'cannot create examples that do not exist'. Research Directions (8 October 2026) reports its outcome as 39.8% of L6 bodies on 376 held-out renders, and separately counts zero verified transitional persons on real frames. The two statements are about renders and real frames and agree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both: the render-based result on 376 transitional patients (39.8% L6, Research Directions) and zero verified real-frame transitional test persons as of 8 October 2026.

verdicts.quote_a: is training now — 18,906 training frames, 56 test specimens
verdicts.quote_b: is being measured directly right now
verdicts.explanation: The two pages describe different runs. The 22 September 2026 page's fleet detector and its sampler A/B have no reported outcome on any page read. The undated physics page's run, a detector trained on renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs, is reported in Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy as the population-matched 90-97%. So one run is resolved and the other is not.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the population-matched 90-97% as the outcome of the physics page's run. The fleet detector's run record (18,906 frames, 56 test specimens) is needed for the other.

verdicts.quote_a: Use two credentials for two jobs. A one-year token from `claude setup-token`, minted on the laptop and stored on scratch, authenticates every batch and non-interactive run: it never needs refreshing, so a job that starts at 03:00 cannot fail on an expired access token.
verdicts.quote_b: `setup-token` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` injected into jobs (notes 07, 08, 09): forbidden by the credential rule; the student's `claude auth login` is used where it sits.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 2026-10-03. The playbook is a site-agnostic design for one person's subscription on a shared Slurm cluster. It gives every batch run a setup token, because a headless -p run on the login has been reported not to refresh (issue #50743). The roadmap rejects exactly that for Beethoven: its rule is that Beethoven never reads, stores or relays a Claude credential. Instead it uses the student's own login, and phase 0 measures whether a headless batch run works that way. The scopes differ (a person's own deployment against Beethoven's product rule), but for the same kind of run the two prescribe opposite credentials, and the roadmap names and refuses the playbook's choice.
verdicts.resolution_hint: For Beethoven and hpcworker, carry the roadmap's rule: the student's own claude auth login and no setup token in jobs. Cite the playbook's issue #50743 as the risk phase 0 must measure, and keep the setup token only as a generic, non-Beethoven option.

verdicts.quote_a: Keep it one account. Rotating accounts or pooling several users' tokens to widen the window is the behaviour Anthropic's terms prohibit; if the workload needs more than one subscription's window, it is a workload for an API key.
verdicts.quote_b: What the owner already decided. The owner's own several Claude accounts may be coordinated from one orchestrator of the owner's, each worker on one account's token, knowing the terms question.
verdicts.explanation: The playbook (2026-10-03) treats account rotation and pooled tokens as prohibited by the terms ('One account per user, no account rotation, no pooled tokens'). The handoff (2026-10-13) records the owner's decision to coordinate several of their own accounts, made knowing the terms question. It also describes cswap switching accounts at 90 percent and a pool of organization secrets, and says to re-read the Usage Policy that takes effect on 2026-11-12. The review (2026-10-21) runs cloud workers on 'the token pool'. The two pages disagree on one person rotating their own accounts, and the handoff acknowledges the question without settling it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the playbook's reading of the terms beside the owner's dated decision of 2026-10-13, presented as a decision taken knowing that question. The re-read of the Usage Policy effective 2026-11-12, which the handoff makes a step, would settle which stands.

verdicts.quote_a: Make a fine-grained personal access token on your own GitHub account (Settings, Developer settings, Fine-grained tokens) with read access to Contents on OpenSpineConsortium/spine-program only.

It replaces that setup with one classic repo token in ~/.beethoven/git-credentials, read by git's store helper, so the student can push. A fine-grained token is kept only as a fallback, with Contents, Issues and Pull requests at Read and write. Each guide is internally consistent; the later one revises the earlier.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the connect guide's setup: a classic repo token in ~/.beethoven/git-credentials, mode 600, with the fine-grained fallback. Mention the onboarding's read-only token only as the earlier issue-19 probe.

verdicts.explanation: The roadmap states the Wayne State grid's rule, from hpcworker's CLAUDE.md. The playbook's CLAUDE.md is a template for any shared Slurm cluster, with a generic ceiling of one core for 60 seconds and 4 GB. A site rule stricter than a generic ceiling does not contradict it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: For this grid, carry hpcworker's and the lab recipe's rule. Give the playbook's ceiling as a generic default.

verdicts.quote_a: The login node runs only `sbatch`, `squeue`, `scancel`, `ls`, `tail`, `git`. Downloads are jobs too; compute nodes have internet.
verdicts.quote_b: Run these commands in the terminal of your Beethoven session (a compute node), not on the login node, where git has not been tested yet.
verdicts.explanation: The lab recipe (2026-09-27) permits git on the login node. The connect guide (2026-10-14) says it is untested there, and gives an at-once kill as the login-node symptom. Permission is not a measurement, and no page records git running, or being killed, on the login node.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The login-node half of spine-program issue 19 settles it.

verdicts.quote_a: Until issue 19 settles whether the grid can reach GitHub, files travel between them through a clone on your own computer.
verdicts.quote_b: Your Beethoven session already reaches GitHub: it cloned your two public repositories from the compute node.
verdicts.explanation: On 2026-10-13 the onboarding holds the question open and routes files through the student's computer. On 2026-10-14 the connect guide reports that a compute node cloned two public repositories, so reachability is settled. It says only a login was missing; the private read with a token is its step 3 test, not yet reported done.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry that compute nodes reach GitHub, from the connect guide (2026-10-14). The private-repository read with the student's token is the remaining check.

verdicts.quote_a: Make a fine-grained personal access token on your own GitHub account (Settings, Developer settings, Fine-grained tokens) with read access to Contents on OpenSpineConsortium/spine-program only.
verdicts.quote_b: One classic token with the `repo` scope covers spine-program and your own repositories at once.
verdicts.explanation: The onboarding (2026-10-13) sets up a read-only fine-grained token in $HOME/.beethoven/github_token as issue 19's probe. The connect guide (2026-10-14) follows it and replaces it: one classic repo token in ~/.beethoven/git-credentials, read by git's store helper, with a fine-grained token at Read and write as the fallback. This lets the student push. In both, the token is typed by the student and never shown to Claude.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the connect guide's token setup. Mention the onboarding's token only as the earlier probe.

verdicts.quote_a: and the repository holds a link to them in each folder. In a Beethoven session the link opens
verdicts.quote_b: fills once with a script; until he has, those links point at nothing and the files are read from git history
verdicts.explanation: The onboarding (2026-10-13) says the folders live in the shared archive on the grid and that the link opens in a Beethoven session. The connect guide (2026-10-14) says the owner has yet to fill the archive with a script, so the links point at nothing for now. The later page corrects the state; whether the archive has been filled since is not recorded.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the connect guide's state as of 2026-10-14. A look at the shared spine-program archive folder settles whether it has since been filled.

verdicts.quote_a: adds it to the testers group and adds your AccessID to the lab volume's access list
verdicts.quote_b: **Visibility Public** (this is the change from 19.0.0), **Trusted testers empty** (the Beethoven-users group served the private listing and is retired)
verdicts.explanation: On the same day, 2026-10-13, the onboarding admits a student through the testers group, and the store page makes 20.0.0's listing public. That page empties the trusted testers and retires the group, leaving the access service's approval check to decide who can use the extension. The store change waits on the owner's hand upload and Google's review, and no page records that they happened.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Once the public listing is live, carry the store page's route: install from the store, admitted by the approval check. The dashboard's record of the 20.0.0 review settles which route held when.

verdicts.quote_a: Private, the way Beethoven is published, works as well: it then wants the testers' Google Group address, and only its members can open the listing.
verdicts.quote_b: Distribution set to Public with no trusted testers
verdicts.explanation: On 2026-10-08 Beethoven is published Private, behind a testers' group. On 2026-10-13 the store page has the owner set 20.0.0's Distribution to Public, with no trusted testers. The private state no longer holds once that upload goes through; neither page records the review's outcome.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Public with no trusted testers from 20.0.0 (store page, 2026-10-13), marked as pending the review's outcome until the dashboard confirms it.

verdicts.quote_a: Keep it one account. Rotating accounts or pooling several users' tokens to widen the window is the behaviour Anthropic's terms prohibit
verdicts.quote_b: `hpcworker accounts start N NAME` starts a worker of its own on Claude account slot N.
verdicts.explanation: The playbook (2026-10-03) holds one account per user, with no rotation, under its reading of the terms; the roadmap and checklist keep 'one person, one account'. The plan of 2026-10-21 runs projects on several Claude account slots of one person: the Wayne State Max account now, and a gmail account to make it two. The positions differ. The handoff records the owner deciding this for their own accounts, knowing the terms question.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the owner's decision of 2026-10-13 on their own accounts, the playbook's reading of the terms beside it, and the re-read of the Usage Policy due before 2026-11-12.

verdicts.quote_a: Since framework 22 the grid runs several named workers at once, each one a Remote Control environment.
verdicts.quote_b: Two or more grid workers running at once on real nodes: no second worker has been started, since that spends allocation and waits on your word and a number.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are dated 2026-10-21. The plan states as fact that framework 22 runs several named workers at once. The review, read at 12:03 UTC, lists one worker online and records two at once on real nodes as never tried. The plan's own open questions (shared accounts, resume) show it was not measured either. The design supports it; running it is unrecorded.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the review's wording: framework 22 starts each named worker as its own job, but two at once on real nodes has not been run.

verdicts.quote_a: nothing yet plans research, runs it headless or enforces REFORMS.
verdicts.quote_b: Runs one `claude -p … --output-format stream-json` per request, up to `--concurrency` (default 2), with a 6 h cap.
verdicts.explanation: The roadmap's 'nothing yet' is scoped to its two repositories, hpcworker and beethoven-extension. The headless daemon the plan describes belongs to Beethoven for VS Code (beethoven-vscode grid/beethovend.js), a separate edition. That edition also allows --dangerously-skip-permissions, which hpcworker's contract refuses. The two statements are about different code.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the roadmap's statement for hpcworker and the extension. Cite the VS Code daemon as prior evidence for phase 0's question, not as hpcworker capability.

verdicts.quote_a: tagged `v2.0.0` at its merge commit (53d5ae5) on 2026-10-07. A session may not create tags.
verdicts.quote_b: Version 5.0.0 on main, untagged (the last tag, v3.0.0, is what both consumers pin)
verdicts.explanation: On 2026-10-07 the consumers pin v2.0.0. By 2026-10-15 the spec has main at 5.0.0 untagged, with the consumers on v3.0.0. The handoff of 2026-10-13 agrees: only v1.0.0 to v3.0.0 are tagged.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the consumers' pin v3.0.0, with main at 5.0.0 untagged, as of 2026-10-15.

verdicts.quote_a: no counterexample from the symbolic check (11 minutes 39 seconds on 4 cores)
verdicts.quote_b: Mostly a bounded search: 13 of 165 conditions confirmed over all paths, 152 not confirmed within the bound, on 5.0.0's tree (14 min 3 s on 4 cores)
verdicts.explanation: The two figures are of different trees, qa #4's commit (2.0.0) and 5.0.0, and they measure different things. One finds no counterexample; the other counts conditions confirmed over all paths. Both can hold at once: a bounded search can find no counterexample while confirming only 13 of 165 conditions. The later page does not revise the earlier number; it reads the check more precisely.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the handoff's reading on 5.0.0: a bounded search, 13 of 165 confirmed over all paths. Note that 'no counterexample' is not a proof.

verdicts.quote_a: CI minutes now come from the organization's Actions quota: 2,000 a month on a Free organization, 3,000 on Team.
verdicts.quote_b: Your organization is on Enterprise Cloud, so every rule, review, environment and attestation is included in its private and internal repositories.
verdicts.explanation: The store page (2026-10-08) gives only the Free and Team quotas for OpenSpineConsortium and warns about moving into a Free organization, without saying which plan the organization is on. The handoff (2026-10-13) states the organization is on Enterprise Cloud. From github/docs it lists internal visibility and 50,000 included minutes as Enterprise Cloud features. The later page gives the plan the earlier one left out.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Enterprise Cloud, with its 50,000 included minutes, from the handoff. The organization's billing page would confirm it.

verdicts.quote_a: Leave it unset until the 20.0.0 upload by hand is done, so the first automatic draft does not land on top of it.
verdicts.quote_b: This needs a store release.
verdicts.explanation: The store page (2026-10-13) leaves the 20.0.0 hand upload, and with it the CWS_ON_PUSH switch, to the owner. The plan of 2026-10-21 has Beethoven at 23.x and says its next feature needs a store release. It does not say whether 20.0.0 was uploaded, whether review passed or whether automatic releases are on.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The Chrome Web Store dashboard's item history, and the CWS_ON_PUSH variable in beethoven-extension's settings, settle it.

verdicts.quote_a: beethoven-agents and beethoven-research have open pull requests, and the standard itself is merged in the hub as `INTERFACES.md`.
verdicts.quote_b: merged on 2026-10-07 with every check green
verdicts.explanation: The encapsulation page's opening paragraph says the two repositories have open pull requests. Its own 'What lands next' item 4, and its pull-request table, say beethoven-agents #4 and beethoven-research #6 merged on 2026-10-07 with every check green. Its bold 'What the owner does next' line also says they are re-pinned and merged. The opening line is stale within the page.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 'merged on 2026-10-07' from the page's body and table.

verdicts.quote_a: Whether `--continue` keeps the session across it is not yet measured (`hpcworker:docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md:22`)
verdicts.quote_b: Whether a successor job's `--continue` keeps a long session whole across several job ends.
verdicts.explanation: The plan (2026-10-07) and the review (2026-10-21) both list it as not measured, the review under its 'Not measured yet' heading. The plan of 2026-10-21 asks the same of the Work locally pairing. The earlier statement still holds, so it is not stale.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 'not measured' as of 2026-10-21. A measured successor resume would close it.

verdicts.quote_a: Multi-run dashboard, per-site setup checks, store release
verdicts.quote_b: The listing's images on the dashboard are 9.0.0's.
verdicts.explanation: The store page shows the extension was on the store before the roadmap's phases: it reuses 19.0.0's privacy answers and 9.0.0's images, and the page of 2026-10-08 says Beethoven is published Private. The roadmap's phase 5 store release is the release of the engine's multi-run version. The transport layer's 20.0.0 upload on 2026-10-13 is not that release, so it does not break the phases' order.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the roadmap's phase 5 store release as the engine's release, and the 20.0.0 public listing as a separate release of the launcher.

verdicts.quote_a: most compute nodes cannot reach the internet directly; Claude Code needs `api.anthropic.com` on every turn, so the job must run on a partition with egress or through the site's HTTPS proxy.
verdicts.quote_b: Downloads are jobs too; compute nodes have internet.
verdicts.explanation: The playbook speaks of 'most' clusters and allows for a partition with egress. The lab recipe states Wayne State's fact, and the connect guide's clone from a compute node on 2026-10-14 bears it out. A generic statement and a site's exception do not contradict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry that Wayne State's compute nodes have internet, from the lab recipe and the connect guide.

verdicts.quote_a: apptainer build --fakeroot --build-arg CLAUDE_VERSION=2.1.271 claude-code.sif claude-code.def
verdicts.quote_b: installs Claude Code 2.1.283 into `$ROOT/npm`
verdicts.explanation: The playbook's 2.1.271 is the build argument of its own example image, and it says to rebuild from the current stable channel. The plan's 2.1.283 is what VS Code's bootstrap.sbatch installs into the lab's image (beethoven-vscode 631226e, 2026-10-07). The two pins are for different images, so the later does not make the earlier stale.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 2.1.283 for the Wayne lab image as of 2026-10-07, from the plan. Give 2.1.271 only as the playbook's example.

verdicts.quote_a: a consent screen left in Testing gives refresh tokens that expire after seven days, and the workflow would start failing a week later.
verdicts.quote_b: a token made while the app is in Testing stops working seven days after you authorized it.
verdicts.explanation: Both store guides (2026-10-13 and 2026-10-08) give the seven-day Testing lifetime and the six-months-unused lifetime of a refresh token. The 2026-10-08 guide adds Google deleting an OAuth client unused for six months, with an e-mail 30 days before. The 2026-10-13 page links Google's Chrome Web Store API page for the setup steps, but neither page cites a source for the lifetimes.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Google's OAuth documentation on refresh-token expiry would source the seven-day and six-month figures.

verdicts.quote_a: **After the review** (usually one to three days, by e-mail to the dashboard's account)
verdicts.quote_b: Review of a first item with `nativeMessaging` and `scripting` usually takes several days; you get an email either way.
verdicts.explanation: The two pages do not carry one claim. The 2026-10-08 page speaks of a first item with nativeMessaging and scripting, for claude-swap-cloud. The 2026-10-13 page speaks of a new version of the existing Beethoven item. The figures differ with that scope. Both are unsourced estimates.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each as an unsourced estimate with its scope, or source both from the Chrome Web Store's review-time documentation.

verdicts.quote_a: the version becomes `<manifest version>.<number of commits on main>`, for example 20.0.0.312.
verdicts.quote_b: The item starts at that version, 0.2.0 followed by the commit count, so every later build from main is above it.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages describe the same release kit, OpenSpineConsortium/chrome-store-release-kit, for two extensions. It has the same four-part version (manifest version plus commit count), the same five CWS_ secrets with the OAuth Playground refresh token, and the same CWS_ON_PUSH upload or publish switch. This is one mechanism described twice, not two confirmations.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the mechanism once, cited to the release kit's README, with each extension's example version.

verdicts.quote_a: The repositories' standing rules (both `CLAUDE.md` files) already decide several things the project topic leaves open.
verdicts.quote_b: the framework is held to bash 4.2 and Python 3.6 standard library (the CentOS 7 login node)
verdicts.explanation: The roadmap attributes its rules table, including 'Framework: bash 4.2 and Python 3.6 standard library on the login node', to both repositories' CLAUDE.md files, which its Summary dates to hpcworker 2e5bcf8. So the claim has a source on that page. The checklist repeats it without a source.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it cited to hpcworker's CLAUDE.md at 2e5bcf8, as the roadmap does. The CentOS 7 detail comes from the checklist.

verdicts.quote_a: The notes assume Lustre; Wayne State is CephFS with a Panasas home, which changes none of the node-local scratch advice.
verdicts.quote_b: Large outputs on the lab's CephFS volume, not home. Home is a soft quota read with `pan_quota`.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages put the lab volume on CephFS, and neither cites a source for the filesystems. Only the roadmap names a Panasas home; the lab recipe implies it through pan_quota without saying so.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Wayne State's research-computing documentation, or a mount listing on the grid, would source CephFS for the lab volume and Panasas for home.

verdicts.quote_a: Remote Control is unavailable under the HIPAA configuration and stores transcripts on Anthropic's servers
verdicts.quote_b: A token typed into a Remote Control conversation becomes part of the transcript, which hpcworker's own notice says Anthropic stores (`hpcworker:1150-1152`).
verdicts.explanation: The spec's risk 9 gives no source. The plan does cite one for transcript storage: hpcworker's own notice at lines 1150-1152. That is a secondary source, not Anthropic's own page, but the claim is not unsourced on these pages. The HIPAA part is the spec's alone, without a source.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry transcript storage cited to hpcworker's notice as the plan does, and seek Anthropic's Remote Control documentation for it and for the HIPAA statement.

verdicts.quote_a: A cloud worker stopped at its 90 minute limit keeps only what it pushed
verdicts.quote_b: each six-hourly run or queued issue can start six 90-minute runs
verdicts.explanation: The review (2026-10-21) and the handoff (2026-10-13) both rest on a 90-minute limit per cloud worker run. Neither cites workers.yml or a timeout value. The handoff's only mention of 90 minutes is this recommendation line.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The timeout in symphony-template's .github/workflows/workers.yml would source the 90 minutes.

verdicts.quote_a: All 32 REFORMS items can be tied to a gate, but only 20 can be verified by code; the other 12 can only be required as a written field the gate refuses to see empty.
verdicts.quote_b: REFORMS (32 items, 20 as code gates and 12 declared)
verdicts.explanation: The checklist's own table is the source of the split. It has 32 rows, 1a to 8b, from the REFORMS paper, 12 of them marked Declared (1a, 1b, 1c, 3b, 3c, 3g, 5b, 5f, 6c, 7c, 8a, 8b) and 20 Code. The figure is derived on the page, not unsourced. The spec repeats it, which is one claim, not a second confirmation.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the 32, 20 and 12 split cited to the checklist's table, presented as its design judgement. Note that the spec's figure is a repeat.

verdicts.quote_a: long runs chain with `afterany`, never `afterok`.
verdicts.quote_b: `--dependency=afterany`, never `afterok`; the child reads a file to decide whether the parent succeeded.
verdicts.explanation: The roadmap restates hpcworker's rule from its CLAUDE.md, and the lab recipe gives the same rule with its incident: an 8 h limit left a whole chain DependencyNeverSatisfied on 2026-09-09. It is one rule of the lab, carried in two places.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the rule once, with the lab recipe's incident as its reason.

verdicts.quote_a: a mode-0600 file the job reads, never in `sbatch --export`, logs or the manifest, and never in the extension.
verdicts.quote_b: publication tokens as mode-0600 files, never in argv
verdicts.explanation: Both pages are by the same account on 2026-10-03. Both keep Zenodo and Hugging Face tokens in a mode-0600 file, never on argv or in sbatch --export. Both have the irreversible publish wait for the student's press: the roadmap says 'Drafts prepared automatically; the irreversible publish waits for the student'. It is one rule repeated.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the rule once. The checklist's wording is the fuller one: never in sbatch --export, logs, the manifest or the extension.

clusters.cluster: Detectors, architecture and the training plan

verdicts.quote_a: VinDr-SpineXR requires a personal PhysioNet credentialed account — CITI training plus supervisor attestation, typically weeks.
verdicts.quote_b: One correction to the earlier report. VinDr-SpineXR was described as needing PhysioNet credentialing (CITI training, supervisor sign-off, weeks). It does not. It is a restricted -access dataset: register on PhysioNet, sign the Data Use Agreement, download. Same day.
verdicts.explanation: The field report (undated) says VinDr-SpineXR needs a credentialed PhysioNet account, which takes weeks. The X-ray data handoff, checked on 3 September 2026, names that report as earlier and corrects it: the dataset is restricted access, under the PhysioNet Restricted Health Data DUA 1.5.0, and can be had the same day. The board of 2026-09-11 also lists VinDr as PhysioNet Restricted 1.5.0.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the handoff's statement: VinDr-SpineXR is restricted access, needing a registered user and a signed DUA (PhysioNet Restricted Health Data DUA 1.5.0), obtainable the same day.

verdicts.quote_a: the 4,963 images sit behind a SciDB browser session; four candidate API endpoints all returned errors.
verdicts.quote_b: Eight guessed API endpoints were tried ( sdb-file/file/list , sdb-core/dataSetFile/list , sdb-open/dataset/… and others); all returned errors.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages describe the same failed attempt to download CSXA from Science Data Bank. The field report counts four endpoints. The handoff of 2026-09-03 follows that report: it quotes the report's own line, says its failure text comes from the run's log, and counts eight. It does not say outright that the four was wrong.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry eight guessed endpoints from the X-ray data handoff (2026-09-03), which was checked against the grid and the run log. Note that the field report said four.

verdicts.quote_a: One network, four heads — not separate models, not one flat class list
verdicts.quote_b: single-vertebra ResNets on 96 px targets with a marker channel; BiGRU run labeller per model and rung; flip TTA; entropy for the queue
verdicts.explanation: The decisions page marks a shared backbone as locked, with detection plus keypoints, level, lesion and Cobb heads. The board of 2026-09-11 says the same. The FluoroCap map of 2026-09-14 builds separate models: a YOLO11 pose corner detector, a 4-model level ensemble of single-vertebra ResNets with a BiGRU, and a separate orientation net. The handoff of 2026-10-08 likewise lists five separately trained pieces. No page says the locked decision was revised.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the built system as the handoff (2026-10-08) describes it: separate detectors, an encoder and a recurrent head. Record one network with four heads as the earlier locked design, which was not implemented.

verdicts.quote_a: Give the sacrum its own model. It is not a four-cornered body and should not be asked of a model trained on four-cornered bodies.
verdicts.quote_b: One network, four heads — not separate models, not one flat class list
verdicts.explanation: The naming note of 18 September 2026 decides on a separate single-class sacrum detector, trained on 4,526 images. The decisions page, contemporary with the board of 2026-09-11, locks one network with heads and 'not separate models'. Neither page refers to the other's choice.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the separate sacrum detector of the naming note (2026-09-18) as the later design, and record the one-network decision as superseded in practice. The handoff's 2026-10-08 list of pieces supports separate detectors.

verdicts.quote_a: Name from morphology, never from a count.
verdicts.quote_b: The proposal is to count, not to name. ... nothing learned decides the level.
verdicts.explanation: The naming note (2026-09-18) names each vertebra from its appearance and says nothing is counted. The counting-levels proposal (September 2026, citing runs of 21 September) states the opposite principle: count from an anchor, with no name formed. The handoff (2026-10-08) and the research directions combine the two: 'the count alone names 97.0 %' and coupling adds 1.2 points.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the latest account, from the handoff and research directions of 2026-10-08: per-vertebra naming plus a count from the detected sacrum, with disagreement as the stop signal. State that the earlier pages took opposite single principles.

verdicts.quote_a: Under the matched convention the C-ArmLSpine-held-out vertebra recall is 90.6%.
verdicts.quote_b: held-out-device detection recall 80.5 %; same-device plateau about 84 %
verdicts.explanation: The OR ledger (2026-09-22) re-scored 56 whole C-ArmLSpine frames (287 vertebrae) at outline IoU 0.5 and conf 0.25 and got 90.6%. The handoff (2026-10-08) catalogs held-out-device recall at 80.5% and says its results catalog wins wherever another file differs. The any-view plan (2026-10-21) repeats 80.5%, and 84.0% with 24 device frames added. Neither later page states the truth convention.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 80.5% held-out-device recall, and about 84% with device frames, from the handoff's results catalog. Keep 90.6% only as the ledger's earlier matched-convention rescore, and read the catalog row for its convention.

verdicts.quote_a: | Detection from renders alone | | 0.3% |
verdicts.quote_b: The render-only detector reads 31.7% outline / 54.7% centre.
verdicts.explanation: The OR ledger (2026-09-22) gives the render-only detector on 56 C-ArmLSpine whole frames several values: 17.1% vertebra recall in its device table, 2.4% by body IoU in the rescore, 31.7% by outline and 54.7% by the centre rule. The ledger disagrees with itself on the body-box value. The any-view plan (2026-10-21) gives 0.3%, with no convention, threshold or render generation.
verdicts.resolution_hint: The results catalog row for render-only detection on C-ArmLSpine, giving its truth convention, threshold and render generation, would decide which value to carry.

verdicts.quote_a: A detector trained on renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs finds the sacrum on 90–97% of the real frames, six specimens held out in turn.
verdicts.quote_b: A detector trained only on calibrated renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs finds the sacrum on about 96–98% of real frames (leave-one-specimen-out).
verdicts.explanation: Both pages describe the same population-matched experiment. The counting-levels proposal (September 2026; leave-one-specimen-out runs of 21 September) reports 90–97% in its table of 6 specimens with 3 seeds each. The AIDaS proposal (October 2026) copies much of that text but gives about 96–98% and names no run. The OR ledger separately gives 88.5–91.3% for one specimen's clean render-only number.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 90–97% from counting-levels, which is tied to the 21 September runs and the report tool, unless the leave-one-specimen-out report shows the 96–98% that AIDaS gives.

verdicts.quote_a: our renderer explains 80.9% of a real frame's variance; nine calibrated device terms add 4.3 points, held out by specimen
verdicts.quote_b: The stored DeepFluoro frames also turned out to be log-compressed display images; read correctly, physics alone explains 86% of a real frame rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one.
verdicts.explanation: The ninety-three-pixels board (2026-09-21) gives 80.9% and +4.3. The counting-levels proposal (September 2026) corrects the physics-only share to 86% and the calibrated renderer to about 90%, after finding that the stored frames were log-compressed. The AIDaS proposal is later (October 2026, due 16 October) yet still carries the uncorrected 80.9% and +4.3. So the later page is the stale one.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 86% from physics alone and about 90% from the calibrated renderer, per the counting-levels correction. Mark 80.9% and +4.3 as figures from before the frames were read correctly.

verdicts.quote_a: what is left is a smooth per-frame field with nothing local in it — 0.4% of variance at ≤2 px
verdicts.quote_b: "Nothing local" was too strong ... After the field, the 2–16 px bands sit at 0.1–0.8% of the frame's variance each — two to seven times the noise floor, not at it.
