clusters.cluster: Renders, physics and the sim-to-real gap

verdicts.quote_a: The DRR at the registered pose is a by-product you get for free, but training on the real frame beats training on that DRR (4.89 vs 7.83 mm landmarks on DeepFluoro, Rapuri 2026 ).
verdicts.quote_b: DRRs with ±2.5° view augmentation were the best arm at every threshold ( 4.87 / 6.02 / 9.73 ). A generator wins where the detector is already confident and loses where it is not; physics plus pose augmentation wins everywhere.
verdicts.explanation: Both pages read the same Rapuri 2026 Table 1 and give the same values for the same arms: real-frame training 4.89 mm, DRRs of the real CTs at the registered pose 7.83 mm (What Is Left gives 7.83 for physics DRRs too). Lift Before Label (15 Sep 2026) compares only the unaugmented DRR twin with the real frame; What Is Left adds a third arm, DRRs with ±2.5° view augmentation at 4.87. The numbers do not conflict; the pages compare different arms.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry all three arms from What Is Left's reading of Table 1: real 4.89, unaugmented DRR 7.83, pose-augmented DRR 4.87 (6.02 / 9.73 at the other thresholds). Qualify Lift Before Label's 'real beats DRR' as true only against the unaugmented DRR.

verdicts.quote_a: 80.9% of a real frame's attenuation variance (NCC 0.899)
verdicts.quote_b: The stored DeepFluoro frames also turned out to be log-compressed display images; read correctly, physics alone explains 86% of a real frame rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one.
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep 2026, 03:3x) gives physics alone at 80.9%. Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy (September 2026) uses the leave-one-specimen-out runs of 21 September and revises that figure in its own words: once the frames are read as log-compressed display images, physics alone explains 86% 'rather than 80%'. Its 'about 90% of a held-out one' is for the calibrated renderer on a held-out frame, which is not the same quantity as Ninety-Three's 93.9% with a per-frame surface.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 86% for physics alone and about 90% for the calibrated renderer on a held-out frame, both from Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy. Keep 80.9% only as the figure from before the log-compression correction.

verdicts.quote_a: our renderer explains 80.9% of a real frame's variance; nine calibrated device terms add 4.3 points, held out by specimen; a per-frame smooth field reaches 93.9% against a 99.5% quantum-noise ceiling
verdicts.quote_b: read correctly, physics alone explains 86% of a real frame rather than 80%, and the calibrated renderer about 90% of a held-out one.
verdicts.explanation: The AIDaS proposal (October 2026, due 16 Oct) still gives 80.9%, which is the figure Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy (runs of 21 Sep) had already corrected to 86% after reading the frames as log-compressed images. The later proposal does not mention the correction. The Retrospective Fluoroscopy Protocol repeats 80.9% and 93.9% as well. On physics-only variance explained, the two pages disagree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 86% physics-only (calibrated renderer about 90% held out) from Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy. Flag the proposal and the IRB draft's 80.9% as uncorrected.

verdicts.quote_a: 0.4% of variance at ≤2 px — so there is nothing for a regional network to learn.
verdicts.quote_b: After the field, the 2–16 px bands sit at 0.1–0.8% of the frame's variance each — two to seven times the noise floor, not at it.
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep) says the residual is a smooth per-frame field with nothing local in it. What Is Left After Physics (dated only 2026) takes that exact claim apart on four real frames and states that '"Nothing local" was too strong': after the field, the 2–16 px bands hold 0.1–0.8% of variance, two to seven times the noise floor. The bands differ (≤2 px against 2–16 px), but the later page explicitly revises the conclusion.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry What Is Left's reading: after the smooth field, 0.1–0.8% of variance per band at 2–16 px, two to seven times the noise floor, at cortical edges and bowel gas. Drop 'nothing local'.

verdicts.quote_a: The edge lines are the real frame being sharper than the render: the CT is 1 mm voxels magnified 1.5× onto 0.19 mm pixels, and a render cannot hold detail the CT never had.
verdicts.quote_b: What remains below 8 px is under one percent of variance per band, at cortical edges the 1 mm CT does not resolve.
verdicts.explanation: What Is Left decomposes the residual left after the smooth field by spatial scale. Counting Levels measures the calibrated render's residual by region, with the collimator border kept apart: the border ring holds about two thirds, and inside it cortical edges agree within a few grey levels. Counting Levels also carries What Is Left's attribution itself (sub-percent variance at cortical edges the 1 mm CT does not resolve). The thin-bone deficit it withdraws is not a claim What Is Left makes. These are two measurements that fit together.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both: per-band residual after the field from What Is Left; the region split from Counting Levels (border ring about two thirds of the render residual, cortical edges within a few grey levels inside it).

verdicts.quote_a: A detector trained on renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs finds the sacrum on 90–97% of the real frames, six specimens held out in turn.
verdicts.quote_b: A detector trained only on calibrated renders of DeepFluoro's own CTs finds the sacrum on about 96–98% of real frames (leave-one-specimen-out).
verdicts.explanation: Both pages describe the same population-matched, leave-one-specimen-out detector. Counting Levels (September 2026; table: six specimens, three seeds each) gives 90–97%; the AIDaS proposal (October 2026) gives about 96–98%. Its neighbouring figures (64–77%, the 26-point seed spread, the 5–60% prior) are identical to Counting Levels. Neither page says a later run changed the range, so they disagree. The IRB draft repeats 96–98%.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 90–97% from Counting Levels, which names its runs (21 Sep, tools/deepfluoro_anchor_report.py), unless a later run record shows 96–98%. Check that report's output.

verdicts.quote_a: The clean render-only number for that specimen is 88.5–91.3% at conf 0.05 (three seeds).
verdicts.quote_b: a detector trained only on calibrated renders of that dataset's own CTs finds the sacrum on about 96–98% of real frames
verdicts.explanation: The OR Readiness Ledger (22 Sep) gives 88.5–91.3% for one specimen (18-1109) at conf 0.05 over three seeds. It does not say whether that render-only detector was trained on DeepFluoro's own CTs or on living whole-body CTs, and its other render-only cell for that specimen (v2 generation) is 55.6%. The IRB draft's 96–98% is a range across leave-one-specimen-out folds, threshold unstated. Scope, training population and threshold all differ, and the pages leave them open.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the run record behind the ledger's 88.5–91.3% (which training renders, which threshold) and the per-specimen values behind 96–98%.

verdicts.quote_b: The manuscript's 76.9% belongs to the anchor_none_r2 generation; the v2 generation every real fine-tune started from pools to 64.0%.
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep) reports 76.9% pooled over 365 real frames. The OR Readiness Ledger (22 Sep) does not withdraw it; it assigns it to the anchor_none_r2 generation and gives 64.0% for the v2 generation, with 55.6% on 18-1109. Counting Levels carries both generations together ('64% / 77%', two renderings of the protocol). Read with their generations, the values agree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both with their generation: 76.9% (anchor_none_r2) and 64.0% (v2, the init of every real fine-tune), from the OR Readiness Ledger.

verdicts.quote_a: Scatter width boxed to 6–16 px: +4.3 , 15.8 px with spread 0.4
verdicts.quote_b: | Siemens Cios Fusion (DeepFluoro) | | 366 | | 0.899 → 0.905 (+1.3) |
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels gives +4.3 points of variance explained for the nine terms on top of 80.9% (NCC 0.899). The ledger's Cios Fusion card gives 'held-out R² physics → fitted' as 0.899 → 0.905 (+1.3). The card's baseline equals Ninety-Three's NCC, not its 80.9%. Its own endpoints differ by 0.6 points, not 1.3. Yet the ledger says the fit reproduces the shipped calibration folds to 1e-3 per term. The metric and how folds are combined are not stated, so the gap cannot be read.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the device card file (docs/devices for the Cios Fusion) and its fit log, which state the metric and fold aggregation behind +1.3. Until then carry +4.3 (median +4.1) from Ninety-Three Pixels.

verdicts.quote_a: calibrated , not learned, and it transfers to whole-spine CTs because every fitted term belongs to the device.
verdicts.quote_b: Until this box passes, the claim that physics-styled synthetic frames match real ones is not made.
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels claims the CT-to-fluoroscopy map was calibrated rather than learned, and that it carries over to other CTs on the same device. The ledger (22 Sep) withholds a different claim: that frames styled by sampling a device card are statistically inside the real domain (NPS 0.111 against a 0.015 floor). It does not dispute that the terms were calibrated. Calibrated and statistically matched are separate claims.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both: the nine terms are calibrated to the Cios Fusion (Ninety-Three Pixels), and styled frames are not yet statistically matched (NPS 0.111 vs 0.015, OR Readiness Ledger).

verdicts.quote_a: Your renderer is already here; check its randomisation list against SyntheX’s before adding anything.
verdicts.quote_b: A clip meant to stop implausible draws was applied to 8–11 correlated terms at once, and it saturates rather than truncates
verdicts.explanation: Lift Before Label (15 Sep) speaks of the renderer's physics and asks for its randomisation list to be checked. Counting From The Sacrum (22 Sep) audits the device-card sampler, which the ledger shows was built on 22 Sep, after Lift was written. The two statements are about different things at different times. Separately, Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep) calls strong domain randomisation 'The lever you had not pulled; now built and training'. That page, not the sampler audit, is what corrects Lift's 'already here' on randomisation.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry: physics at the DeepDRR level, strong randomisation added about 21 Sep (Ninety-Three Pixels), and the device-card sampler reaching only 1.7–5.1% of the joint distribution, with a replacement not adopted (Counting From The Sacrum).

verdicts.quote_a: | Detection from renders alone | | 0.3% | | Detection does not transfer from today's renders. |
verdicts.quote_b: The render-only detector reads 31.7% outline / 54.7% centre.
verdicts.explanation: The Any-View Spine Plan (21 Oct) gives 0.3% for render-only detection on C-ArmLSpine and states no metric, convention or threshold. The ledger (22 Sep) gives the render-only detector on the same whole frames as 17.1% (best-F1 threshold), 2.4% body IoU, 31.7% outline and 54.7% centre rule at conf 0.25. The ledger itself shows the value moving tenfold with the box convention. Neither page lets 0.3% be matched to one of its cells or to a later run.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the record the plan cites (docs/research/ct-priors-for-2d-detection.md), naming the detector, truth convention and threshold behind 0.3%.

verdicts.quote_a: sacrum found 83.9%, vertebra recall 90.6% on whole frames once truth boxes use one convention
verdicts.quote_b: | Detection with other devices' real frames plus renders | | 80.5% | | Real frames from any device carry most of it. |
verdicts.explanation: The ledger's 83.9% sacrum and 90.6% vertebra recall come from the rx_lodo detector, trained on the other device families' real frames, rescored under outline truth. The plan's 80.5% is for 'other devices' real frames plus renders' and does not say whether it measures sacrum, vertebrae or another quantity, or under which convention. The arms may differ (renders added) and the metric is unstated.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the run record behind the plan's 80.5% and 84.0% (metric, convention, training mix). Until then carry the ledger's 83.9% sacrum and 90.6% vertebra recall (outline truth).

verdicts.quote_a: | Lateral, whole frame 141 cases, 617 vertebrae, 5-fold CV | | 98.22% | | 100% |
verdicts.quote_b: | Naming, lateral, encoder that saw the device only through renders | | 96.4% (595/617) | | Naming transfers from 3D renders. It is within a point of the 97.4% fine-tuned on the device. |
verdicts.explanation: Counting From The Sacrum (22 Sep) gives 98.22% fine-tuned and 96.27% zero-shot lateral, over 617 vertebrae. The Any-View Spine Plan (21 Oct) gives 97.4% fine-tuned and 96.4% (595/617), the latter for an 'encoder that saw the device only through renders'. The plan is a month later and uses the same denominator, but it does not say it revises the September numbers or that it is the same model. 595/617 is 96.43%, which is not 96.27%.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the plan's cited record (docs/research/ct-priors-for-2d-detection.md) and docs/RSNAI_CLAIMS.json, which show whether 97.4% / 96.4% come from a newer model or replace 98.22% / 96.27%.

verdicts.quote_a: | Zero-shot, AP | | 37.88% | | — |
verdicts.quote_b: | Naming, AP, zero-shot | | 43.7% | | A one-level cranial shift: a counting error, not an appearance error.
verdicts.explanation: Counting From The Sacrum and the ledger (both 22 Sep) give zero-shot AP naming as 37.88% / 37.9%, a one-level cranial shift. The Any-View Spine Plan (21 Oct) gives 43.7% with the same reading. It is later but says neither that this is a new run nor that it corrects the September figure.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the plan's cited record (docs/research/ct-priors-for-2d-detection.md): carry 43.7% if it is a later zero-shot model, otherwise 37.88% from docs/RSNAI_CLAIMS.json.

verdicts.quote_a: | Lateral, whole frame 141 cases, 617 vertebrae, 5-fold CV | | 98.22% | | 100% |
verdicts.quote_b: 98.2% exact level on whole C-ArmLSpine lateral frames, five-fold CV over 148 cases [95.7–100]
verdicts.explanation: Both pages, dated 22 Sep, give the same 98.2% lateral whole-frame result, one over 141 cases and the other over 148. The ledger's split is 105/15/28 = 148 cases. The registry and the plan say 149 cases, and Counting From The Sacrum counts 120 distinct subjects. The pages do not say whether 141 are the cases with a scored lateral frame or whether one count is wrong.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the fold record in docs/RSNAI_CLAIMS.json: the number of cases scored for the lateral whole-frame result, set against the 148 in the split and the 149 in the dataset.

verdicts.quote_a: No per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published at all.
verdicts.quote_b: published class-agnostic C-arm detection reaches 0.96–0.98.
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep), citing its verified literature pass, says no per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy has been published. Counting From The Sacrum (22 Sep) sets its 90.6% per-body recall against 'published class-agnostic C-arm detection' at 0.96–0.98, with no citation on the page. On their face the two statements disagree, and neither page names a source that settles it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry neither without qualification. Find the source behind 0.96–0.98 (docs/RSNAI_CLAIMS.json), and whether it is recall on real C-arm frames, before the textbook states either way.

verdicts.quote_a: The best published registration-free naming is 73.3%, and it imports identity from a preoperative radiograph.
verdicts.quote_b: For learned, CT-free labelling on a real intraoperative modality the best found is 88.3% on 100 cadaver Long-Film images from a network trained only on images synthesised from 297 CTs (Huang 2022
verdicts.explanation: Counting From The Sacrum (22 Sep) names 73.3% as the best published registration-free naming and gives no citation. The FluoroCap Reality Check (15 Sep) names 88.3% (Huang 2022, cadaver Long-Film, trained on synthesised images only) as the best CT-free labelling on a real intraoperative modality. That method uses no registration, so the two 'best' figures conflict. Only the Reality Check sources its figure.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 88.3% (Huang 2022, uninstrumented cadaver Long-Film) from the Reality Check, with its scope. Source the 73.3% or narrow its scope (C-arm frames, patients) before keeping it.

verdicts.quote_a: The LevelCheck failure criterion is a projection-distance error above 20 mm at the detector, about half a thoracolumbar body
verdicts.quote_b: LevelCheck placed labels within PDE < 30 mm on all 398 intraoperative mobile radiographs from 178 patients with a preoperative CT
verdicts.explanation: Lift Before Label gives both a 20 mm failure criterion, tied to gross-failure rates of 11.5% to 5.6%, and '398/398 within 30 mm in the 178-patient series'. The Reality Check gives the 30 mm figure for the 398 radiographs. Both pages agree on the 398 series. Neither says which LevelCheck study uses the 20 mm criterion, so whether the two thresholds belong to different studies cannot be read from the pages.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the LevelCheck papers: which study defines failure at 20 mm PDE and which reports the 398 radiographs at 30 mm. Carry each threshold with its study.

verdicts.quote_a: a phase-recognition model on simulated tools and anatomy scored 93.8% simulated and 67.6% on cadaver ( Pelphix 2023 ).
verdicts.quote_b: Also withdrawn: the planned Pelphix citation. Its 99.2→71.7 is surgical-phase accuracy, not detection.
verdicts.explanation: Lift Before Label (15 Sep) cites Pelphix correctly as a phase-recognition model, as evidence that recognition gaps are wider than geometric ones. Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep) withdraws Pelphix as a comparator for detection, since its figure is surgical-phase accuracy. The Reality Check explains the two number pairs: '93.8-99.2% on simulation to 67.6-71.7%' depending on the version read. The withdrawal applies to a use Lift does not make.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Pelphix as a surgical-phase recognition gap of 93.8–99.2% to 67.6–71.7% on 257 cadaver frames, by version (Reality Check), and never as detection.

verdicts.quote_a: a DRR-only model that collapsed on real frames recovered to F1 0.84 against a 0.86 DRR ceiling with 3,317 registered real crops
verdicts.quote_b: Jecklin 2024 needed 3,317 pose-paired real frames from 10 cadavers to lift lumbar reconstruction from a surface score of 0.08 back to 0.63-0.73, still below its 0.79 DRR ceiling
verdicts.explanation: Lift Before Label (15 Sep, its own verification pass never ran) gives Jecklin 2024 as F1 0.84 against a 0.86 ceiling; elsewhere on the page it gives one case at 8% against 76% on the DRR twin. The Reality Check (same day, after a refuting pass) gives a surface score of 0.08 to 0.63–0.73 against a 0.79 ceiling. These may be different metrics from the same paper, and the Reality Check does not say Lift's F1 is wrong.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with Jecklin 2024's tables: whether F1 0.84 / 0.86 and surface score 0.63–0.73 / 0.79 are both reported. Until then carry the Reality Check's verified surface-score figures.

verdicts.quote_a: Shape-model fitting from two arbitrary views reaches Dice 0.73 on one cadaver and assumes the level rather than inferring it ( Spine-DART 2026 ).
verdicts.quote_b: Spine-DART's lumbar Mask R-CNN trained on >150,000 DRRs from 377 CTs held Dice 0.82 on 35 real fluoroscopy images of one cadaver against 0.89 on DRRs, a 7-point drop, not the 5 first reported
verdicts.explanation: The two pages report different parts of Spine-DART, and each page says which part. Lift gives shape-model fitting from two views (a 3-D result, Dice 0.73). The Reality Check gives the 2-D lumbar Mask R-CNN segmentation on 35 real frames (Dice 0.82 against 0.89 on DRRs). Read by component, they agree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both by component: two-view shape fitting Dice 0.73 (Lift), and 2-D Mask R-CNN 0.82 real against 0.89 DRR, a 7-point drop (Reality Check, verified).

verdicts.quote_a: strong domain randomisation on 10,000 DRRs from 20 CTs beat training on the 366 real frames (5.95 vs 6.46 mm) and CycleGAN or ADDA added nothing on top (SyntheX).
verdicts.quote_b: the scaled-up set is reported as both 10,000 and 18,000 images, that it beat the real-trained model under regular augmentation too so scale rather than the strong-randomisation list is what carried the win, and that the scaling curve is not monotone
verdicts.explanation: Lift Before Label (15 Sep, unverified) credits the 5.95 vs 6.46 mm win to strong domain randomisation on 10,000 DRRs. The Reality Check (same day, refuting pass) says the scaled set is reported as both 10,000 and 18,000, and that scale, not the randomisation list, carried the win. Ninety-Three Pixels backs the split: strong randomisation gives parity (6.44 vs 6.46), and 'Scale — 1k → 10k renders: 6.61 → 5.95 mm.' Lift calls itself a companion to the Reality Check, so neither page plainly comes after the other.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the Reality Check's verified reading: parity at 6.44 vs 6.46 mm under strong randomisation, and 5.95 mm with the scaled set (reported as 10,000 or 18,000), the win coming from scale.

verdicts.quote_a: No diffusion or pix2pix model. DeepFluoro not extended. No volume grafted.
verdicts.quote_b: A RealDRR-style refiner trained on the real pairs, a high-pass-only version of it, and a training-free low-band swap were each trained six folds by three seeds and applied to the living-abdomen renders.
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep, 03:3x) lists learned models among things not done on purpose. Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy, whose numbers come from the runs of 21 September and which revises Ninety-Three's 80% figure, then reports a RealDRR-style refiner, a high-pass refiner and a low-band swap: 72%, 72% and 74% sacrum recall against a 64% baseline, all inside the 26-point seed spread. The later page shows the refiners were built and measured.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Counting Levels' result: refiners and the low-band swap add 8–10 points, each smaller than the seed spread, and the refined render agrees slightly less with the real frame (68.1% vs 69.3%).

verdicts.quote_a: Learned refiners and Fourier low-band swaps are being measured as arms; results are pending.
verdicts.quote_b: the Fourier low-band swap added about ten points, the high-pass refiner and the full refiner about eight — all the same sign, each smaller than the 26-point seed spread, none within fifteen points of the population-matched control.
verdicts.explanation: The AIDaS proposal (October 2026, due 16 Oct) says the refiner and low-band-swap arms are still pending. Counting Levels (September 2026) already reports them measured, stating 'Every synthetic-data number here is from the leave-one-specimen-out runs of 21 September 2026': 72%, 74% and 72%, with the refined render at 68.1% against 69.3%. The proposal's 'pending' was out of date in the record when it was written.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the measured arms from Counting Levels Under Fluoroscopy and mark the proposal's 'results are pending' as stale.

verdicts.quote_a: LO[FluoroGen LoRA\n4 GPUs] -->|weights file| GEN[generation array ×8] --> CHK[geometry check] --> TR[level-model arm with synthetic]
verdicts.quote_b: at 0.2 it leaves the render essentially unchanged, at 0.35 it already smears end-plates and pedicles. There is no usable setting; img2img is dropped.
verdicts.explanation: The Pipeline Map of 14 Sep 2026 draws FluoroGen (SDXL + ControlNet + LoRA) feeding a generation array and a level-model arm. The Overnight Report of 15 Sep says the array was cancelled at 05:50 after 12,896 images, none usable, and that a low-strength sweep found no usable setting, so img2img was dropped. The later report reverses the map.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the Overnight Report (15 Sep): FluoroGen img2img dropped, 12,896 images kept for inspection only. The map's FluoroGen lane is historical.

verdicts.quote_a: A v2 restricted to the 2,991 classifier-verified panels and to renders with at least two unclipped vertebrae is queued (jobs 40285274, 40285275); its number replaces v1's when it lands.
verdicts.quote_b: Do not build a single-view reconstruction stage, a 3-D CT generator, or an img2img translator; the evidence says each costs more than it returns.
verdicts.explanation: On 15 Sep the Reality Check and the Overnight Report both have a CUT v2 translator queued, under different job numbers (40285274/5 against 40285316/7). The same day, Lift Before Label recommends against building an img2img translator, and on 21 Sep Ninety-Three Pixels says 'the DRR→fluoro GAN is measured and buys nothing. It was not built.' No page reports CUT v2's result or says it was cancelled, so whether it ran or still runs is not recorded.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the scheduler record of the CUT v2 jobs (40285274/5 or 40285316/7) and any result file. Until then carry v1 as invalid (trained toward contaminated panels) and v2 as unreported.

verdicts.quote_a: Flat. 836 px to 139 px costs 0.00 points of per-vertebra recall.
verdicts.quote_b: Resolution : 48 → 96 px targets, lumbar one-vertebra 80.7% → 85.4%. Same lever as on CT (73.7% → 82.8%).
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels measures detection: per-vertebra recall of the film detector as whole films are downsampled. The Level Context Ladder (13 Sep) measures level naming of a single crop by its target pixel size. Ninety-Three itself notes that the earlier pixel effect 'was measured on naming panels, not on sweep fields, and on a different task'. The two results are about different tasks and do not conflict.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both by task: resolution does not affect detection down to 139 px (Ninety-Three Pixels); it does affect single-crop naming, 80.7% to 85.4% lumbar at 48 to 96 px (Level Context Ladder).

verdicts.quote_a: 836 px to 139 px costs 0.00 points of per-vertebra recall.
verdicts.quote_b: The crops are upscaled windows, so a detector that never saw this device's frames at that scale loses most of them, while the same-device control keeps 82%.
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three's ladder downsamples whole real films for an in-domain film detector. The ledger's drop (91% to 36% on a three-vertebra field) is for a detector that never saw the device, scored on upscaled crops, and the ledger notes that the same-device control keeps 82%. Coarseness in-domain and magnification on an unseen device are different conditions, and both pages state theirs.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both: downsampling costs nothing in-domain (Ninety-Three Pixels); magnified crops cost a held-out-device detector most of its recall (OR Readiness Ledger).

verdicts.quote_a: no paired-DRR paper in the verified record evaluated that on a downstream task
verdicts.quote_b: Paired cGAN DRR→real rendering ( RealDRR 2020 ) improved image metrics with no downstream number.
verdicts.explanation: What Is Left's claim concerns learned DRR-to-real detail (invented texture) in its verified record. The examples Lift cites against it, Jecklin's pix2pix and the paired-against-unpaired comparison, are real-to-DRR translation or registration success. On the DRR-to-real direction, Lift agrees: RealDRR improved image metrics with no downstream number.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry What Is Left's statement, limited to DRR-to-real generators, with Lift's real-to-DRR results (F1 0.84, at most one point paired vs unpaired) listed separately.

verdicts.quote_a: Budget hundreds to low thousands of registered frames over at least 10–20 patients.
verdicts.quote_b: Target 3,000-5,000 frames from 800-1,500 patients in twelve months at one centre
verdicts.explanation: Lift gives a floor: the registered frames needed before the gap can be expected to close, at least 10–20 patients. The Reality Check gives a collection target for Tier 0 that also supports a 99% evaluation per stratum. A target of thousands of frames from hundreds of patients meets Lift's floor and does not contradict it.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Lift's floor for fine-tuning and the Reality Check's 3,000–5,000 frames from 800–1,500 patients as the collection target, each with its purpose.

verdicts.quote_a: so about 1,100 labelled bodies are needed in the held-out set. (To hold 99% recall to a half-width of 0.5 points would need about 1,520.)
verdicts.quote_b: bounding 99% within ±0.5% takes about 1,500 verified images per stratum you report
verdicts.explanation: The two pages' arithmetic agrees: 99% at ±0.5 points needs about 1,520 (the IRB draft, normal approximation) or about 1,500 (the Reality Check, Wilson). The IRB draft's primary endpoint is 97% at ±1 point overall (about 1,100). The Reality Check applies the 99% bound per stratum, with at least four strata. The endpoints differ; the sample-size figures do not.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry about 1,100 bodies for 97% ±1 point overall (IRB draft). For a 99% claim, about 1,500 per reported stratum, at least four (Reality Check).

verdicts.quote_a: TotalSegmentator, 156 of 1939 with C2 and sacrum.
verdicts.quote_b: line integrals once per geometry from 142 TotalSegmentator whole spines
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels (21 Sep) counts 156 of 1,939 TotalSegmentator subjects that carry C2 and sacrum; the ledger (22 Sep) renders the device corpus from 142 whole spines. The registry gives v3 as 142 whole-spine subjects and 1,935 scans, against a manifest count of 1,939, and Ninety-Three also trains on 48 'clean' subjects. No page states the filter between 156 and 142.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the device-corpus list builder (tools/devcorpus_build.py) or the registry record, which say how 156 became 142 and whether v3 holds 1,935 or 1,939 scans.

verdicts.quote_a: Transitional and corpectomy CT editing on the 802 labelled cases
verdicts.quote_b: The CT axis named 802 abdominopelvic records, which see only the lower spine. It now names every collection here by distinct subject, counted with the same keying the train/validation split uses: TotalSegmentator v3 1,735, v2 1,170, CTSpinoPelvic1K 801
verdicts.explanation: Counting From The Sacrum explains the difference itself: 802 is the count of records or CTs (the registry's 802 CT volumes, release v11), and 801 is the count of distinct subjects under the split's keying. The Ladder's '801 readable cases' and Ninety-Three's 801 renders fit the subject count. These are different units, not a conflict. Whether a release id is one person is still under audit.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 802 CTs and 801 distinct subjects, each named as such, with the open audit of whether an id is one person (Counting From The Sacrum).

verdicts.quote_a: fluorocap_drr | | 2385 | | — | | 677 rows | | 11% | | — | | 72.8% press-degraded
verdicts.quote_b: 29,500 figure panels harvested from the literature; 72.8 percent are reproductions with no pixel residual
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels puts '72.8% press-degraded' in the usability cell of the fluorocap_drr row (2,385 items). The registry (20 Oct) gives 72.8 percent of 29,500 literature panels as reproductions with no pixel residual. It is the same percentage and the same idea, but neither page states the denominator it was measured on, and the panel count changed over time (19,048, 19,581, 29,484, 29,500).
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the measurement record behind 72.8% (the registry cites DATA_MANIFEST defect 35), which gives its denominator and date.

verdicts.quote_a: Images on disk went from 11,349 to 19,048: 17,755 figure panels
verdicts.quote_b: 19,581 (18,119 figure panels, 1,096 video, 366 video-medium) | | find on ~/FluoroCap; morning report's 19,048 superseded
verdicts.explanation: The Overnight Report (15 Sep) gives 19,048 images after round one. The Reality Check, run the same morning by counting files on disk, gives 19,581 and states that the morning report's 19,048 is superseded. Later pages count 29,484 (ledger, 22 Sep) and 29,500 (registry, 20 Oct).
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 19,581 as the 15 Sep count (Reality Check), and 29,500 (registry, 20 Oct) as the latest panel count.

verdicts.quote_a: yes, lumbar, projected from the CBCT (two labellers agreeing on 814 of 910 bodies); 3 real L6 cases
verdicts.quote_b: Level truth for COBRA was rebuilt from two labellers: TotalSegmentator and SPINEPS/VERIDAH agree on 818 of 900 vertebrae (90.9%; 58 disagree, 24 unmatched)
verdicts.explanation: The registry's 814 of 910 is for C-ArmLSpine level truth, projected from its CBCT. The ledger's 818 of 900 is for COBRA. They are two datasets with two separate agreement counts, and nothing on either page conflicts.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both, each with its dataset: C-ArmLSpine 814/910 (registry), COBRA 818/900 (OR Readiness Ledger).

verdicts.quote_a: The detector finds C2 on 99.5% of full renders and 31% of 93-pixel sweep frames.
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three's 99.5% matches its own count 'Its C2 box lands on C2 in 218/219 renders', a check of where the C2 box falls on full renders. The ledger's 85.1% (ws_render) and 88.1% (the 9-class render C2 detector) are recall at conf 0.25, IoU 0.5, on 934 validation renders with C2. Both pages state their sets and measures, and they differ.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry both with their set: C2 box on C2 in 218/219 full renders (Ninety-Three Pixels); C2 recall 85–88% on 934 validation renders, and none on film (OR Readiness Ledger).

verdicts.quote_a: a constant-box location prior scores 5–60%, so these are detection results, not chance
verdicts.quote_b: "Sacrum found" on C-ArmLSpine is therefore partly a statement about layout; vertebra recall and level accuracy are not, and DeepFluoro's sacrum numbers cannot be explained this way.
verdicts.explanation: The proposal's 5–60% prior is for DeepFluoro, and Counting Levels gives the same 5–60% for the population-matched DeepFluoro arm. The ledger's 85.7% layout prior is for C-ArmLSpine, while for DeepFluoro it gives 13.5%, inside 5–60%. It says DeepFluoro's sacrum numbers cannot be explained by layout. On DeepFluoro the two agree.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry the prior by dataset from the ledger (C-ArmLSpine 85.7%, COBRA 58.5%, DeepFluoro 13.5%), and limit 'detection, not chance' to DeepFluoro.

verdicts.quote_a: Two-view fusion in the identifier for frames that come as AP+lateral pairs (the corpus has figure mates; the OR always has both).
verdicts.quote_b: A listhesis or a wedged body seen only on the lateral is invisible on the AP, and a synthesised lateral would paint the typical spine in its place.
verdicts.explanation: Lift says the OR always has both AP and lateral views and recommends two-view fusion. The Any-View plan's warning concerns what a synthesised lateral can show; it never says an operating room lacks laterals. Nothing on the plan's page contradicts Lift's statement.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Lift's recommendation and the plan's warning that a generated lateral is a display aid, not a film. Neither page measures how often an OR frame comes without its mate.

verdicts.quote_a: naive DRRs gave 78.2 mm landmark error, polychromatic multi-material with noise 34.4 , full model 24.7 ; scatter moved only 26.9→24.7.
verdicts.quote_b: naive DRRs to DeepDRR took landmark error on real cadaver films from 78.2 to 24.7 mm ( Unberath 2019 )
verdicts.explanation: What Is Left and Lift Before Label both carry the DeepDRR figure 78.2 to 24.7 mm from Unberath 2019; Ninety-Three Pixels and the Reality Check carry it too. It is one published result restated across pages, not independent confirmations. The breakdowns fit each other (34.4 with polychromatic attenuation; most of the gain before scatter).
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it once, as Unberath 2019: 78.2 to 34.4 to 24.7 mm on 78 real cadaver frames, scatter 26.9 to 24.7 (What Is Left's breakdown).

verdicts.quote_a: CycleGAN scored 6.62 mm and ADDA 6.41 against 6.44 for no adaptation at all
verdicts.quote_b: reached parity with training on real frames ( 6.44 vs 6.46 mm hip landmarks) and with CycleGAN ( 6.62 ) and ADDA ( 6.41 ).
verdicts.explanation: Ninety-Three Pixels and What Is Left carry the same SyntheX figures: CycleGAN 6.62, ADDA 6.41, no adaptation 6.44, real 6.46 mm. What Is Left adds that CycleGAN helped about 1 mm under weak randomisation. This is one published result counted twice.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it once, cited to SyntheX (Gao 2023), with What Is Left's weak-randomisation note.

verdicts.quote_a: A detector trained on real films reaches 99.14% per-body recall on real radiographs; the same architecture trained on renders only reaches 71.67%
verdicts.quote_b: The film-trained detector reaches 99.14% per-body recall on real radiographs; the same architecture trained on synthetic renders reaches 71.67%
verdicts.explanation: The AIDaS proposal and the IRB draft carry the same preliminary-results figures in near-identical wording: 99.14% against 71.67%, exactness 100% to 30.06% on 79 spines, 80.9%, 93.9%/99.5%, 96–98%, 64–77% and the 26-point seed spread. It is one body of claims copied between the two documents. Its DeepFluoro figures also share the staleness noted in candidates 2 and 5.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Treat it as one source. Carry 99.14%/71.67%/30.06% from the manuscript record, and take the DeepFluoro figures from Counting Levels (86%, 90–97%) instead of the copied ones.

verdicts.quote_a: In a registry of 34,544 degenerative spine operations at 27 hospitals (2012–2022) the incidence was 0.12% (95% CI 0.09–0.16)
verdicts.quote_b: In a registry of 34,544 degenerative spine operations across 27 hospitals (2012–2022), the wrong level was operated in 0.12% (95% CI 0.09–0.16)
verdicts.explanation: The proposal and the IRB draft carry the same paragraph with the same figures and the same citations: 34,544 operations, 0.12%, 81.3% disorientation, 51.9 min and 183 mGy per fiducial, $1,750–1,950. Counting Levels restates it as 1 in 830 and 81%. It is one sourced claim repeated, not several.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it once with its citations (Furuya 2026 for the registry, Siminski 2023 and Childers 2018 for the fiducial cost), as the IRB draft gives them.

verdicts.quote_a: surgeons’ error on hard films 30.4%→2.4%, Manbachi 2018
verdicts.quote_b: surgeons' unaided median error on 62 hard radiographs was 30.4%, falling to 2.4% with the overlay
verdicts.explanation: Lift Before Label and the Reality Check both carry LevelCheck's effect on surgeons' error on hard radiographs, 30.4% to 2.4%. The Reality Check adds that it is a median over 62 hard radiographs. It is one published result restated.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it once from the Reality Check's fuller wording (median error, 62 hard radiographs), cited as Manbachi 2018.

verdicts.quote_a: 2,293 vendor frames unused with no written criterion
verdicts.quote_b: 2,293 vendor frames unused. Registration gives their truth.
verdicts.explanation: The registry (20 Oct, in its record data) and the Any-View plan (21 Oct) both say 2,293 of DeepFluoro's 2,659 vendor frames are unused. The plan's table takes its figures from the registry, so this is one count.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry 2,293 of 2,659 vendor frames unused, with no written criterion, once, from the registry.

verdicts.quote_a: synthetic fluoroscopy from CT is close in physics but tuned to one C-arm and one cadaveric population.
verdicts.quote_b: Synthetic fluoroscopy is therefore close in physics but tuned to one C-arm and one population.
verdicts.explanation: The proposal and the IRB draft draw the same conclusion in nearly the same words, from the same DeepFluoro numbers, and neither page gives a source or a second-device measurement for it. It is an inference repeated across two documents, not a sourced finding. Counting Levels states the same limit ('tuned to one C-arm, one protocol and one specimen population').
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it once, as the project's own inference from the DeepFluoro runs. Note that the ledger's later cross-device results (for example 32% on the image intensifier) bear on it.

verdicts.quote_a: COBRA adds full rotations, and renders add unlimited exact pairs.
verdicts.quote_b: The DRR at the registered pose is a by-product you get for free
verdicts.explanation: The two sentences make different claims. The Any-View plan says renders of a CT give any number of exact AP and lateral pairs, and tags the bullet with the registry. Lift says registering a real frame yields its DRR twin at no extra cost, and in the same sentence says that twin is the weaker training data. Each is a property of rendering, not one shared empirical claim.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry each where it belongs. Neither needs an outside source, but Lift's note that the DRR twin trains worse (4.89 vs 7.83 mm) should stay beside it.

verdicts.quote_a: Registration-derived labels are biased toward registration-friendly frames, so a held-out set labelled independently is still needed.
verdicts.explanation: The sentence closes Lift Before Label's section on accuracy and failure modes. Unlike its neighbours, it has no inline citation, and nothing else on the page sources or measures it. The page itself says its numbers were not verified.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry it as an unsourced caution from Lift Before Label. A measurement of label accuracy on frames that register poorly, or a citation, would turn it into a finding.

verdicts.quote_a: Vertebral bodies are large, low-frequency objects and the detector does not need the pixels.
verdicts.quote_b: the discriminating cues for a level (rib on the crop, sacral morphology, transverse-process shape, end-plate contour) are projected features, not depth-ambiguous ones
verdicts.explanation: The two pages make different claims. Ninety-Three's is its reading of a ladder it measured itself: detection recall is flat from 836 to 139 px. Lift's concerns level identity, saying it rests on features visible in projection rather than on depth. One is about how many pixels detection needs, the other about what tells levels apart, so they are not a shared claim.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Ninety-Three's statement with its ladder as evidence. Carry Lift's separately, as an argument, citing Btrfly-net (85–88.5% from projections).

verdicts.quote_a: The direct fix. ~0.3 mm/px with a spacing field, so a 140 mm field is ~470 px.
verdicts.quote_b: Your 0.3% may be the renderer's fault, which is what the physics renderer ablation (#69) tests.
verdicts.explanation: On 21 Sep Ninety-Three Pixels leaves the re-render to the owner. The same page's ladder (option 2) found 'the re-render is not the main event'. The Any-View plan (21 Oct) does not mention re-rendering at C-arm resolution; it puts the render-only shortfall to a physics renderer ablation (#69). No page records the owner's decision on the re-render.
verdicts.resolution_hint: Settle it with the issue record (#69 and any re-render issue) that shows whether the re-render was decided, run or dropped.

verdicts.quote_a: Three direct tests have no number anywhere in the record, and they are next
verdicts.quote_b: the Fourier low-band swap added about ten points
verdicts.explanation: What Is Left lists three tests with no number, the first being FDA's low-band swap as an augmentation on renders, and says the population-matched control 'is being measured directly right now'. Counting Levels, which follows it, reports the population-matched control (90–97%) and a training-free Fourier low-band swap at 74%, about ten points over baseline. verdicts.resolution_hint: Carry Counting Levels' low-band-swap and population-matched results. Keep the other two tests (miss-to-field correlation, dividing out the field at inference) as unmeasured.
